definition: Writing a function as $\mathrm{f}(x) = \ldots$, so that $\mathrm{f}(a)$ means the output when the input is $a$.
The set of input values a function is allowed to take.
The set of output values a function gives from its domain; not the same as the range of a set of data.
The function $\mathrm{f}^{-1}$ that undoes $\mathrm{f}$, taking each output of $\mathrm{f}$ back to its input.
One function applied to the output of another: $\mathrm{gf}(x) = \mathrm{g}(\mathrm{f}(x))$ applies $\mathrm{f}$ first, then $\mathrm{g}$.
